From 9573a365ff9ff45da9222d3fe63695ce562beb24 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Filipe Manana <fdmanana@suse.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:57:43 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] btrfs: log new dentries when logging parent dir of a
 conflicting inode

If we log the parent directory of a conflicting inode, we are not logging
the new dentries of the directory, so when we finish we have the parent
directory's inode marked as logged but we did not log its new dentries.
As a consequence if the parent directory is explicitly fsynced later and
it does not have any new changes since we logged it, the fsync is a no-op
and after a power failure the new dentries are missing.

Example scenario:

  $ mkdir foo

  $ sync

  $rmdir foo

  $ mkdir dir1
  $ mkdir dir2

  # A file with the same name and parent as the directory we just deleted
  # and was persisted in a past transaction. So the deleted directory's
  # inode is a conflicting inode of this new file's inode.
  $ touch foo

  $ ln foo dir2/link

  # The fsync on dir2 will log the parent directory (".") because the
  # conflicting inode (deleted directory) does not exists anymore, but it
  # it does not log its new dentries (dir1).
  $ xfs_io -c "fsync" dir2

  # This fsync on the parent directory is no-op, since the previous fsync
  # logged it (but without logging its new dentries).
  $ xfs_io -c "fsync" .

  <power failure>

  # After log replay dir1 is missing.

Fix this by ensuring we log new dir dentries whenever we log the parent
directory of a no longer existing conflicting inode.

A test case for fstests will follow soon.

Reported-by: Vyacheslav Kovalevsky <slava.kovalevskiy.2014@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-btrfs/182055fa-e9ce-4089-9f5f-4b8a23e8dd91@gmail.com/
Fixes: a3baaf0d786e ("Btrfs: fix fsync after succession of renames and unlink/rmdir")
Reviewed-by: Boris Burkov <boris@bur.io>
Signed-off-by: Filipe Manana <fdmanana@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>

diff --git a/fs/btrfs/tree-log.c b/fs/btrfs/tree-log.c
index e1bd03ebfd98..37c272df52b0 100644
--- a/fs/btrfs/tree-log.c
+++ b/fs/btrfs/tree-log.c
@@ -6195,6 +6195,7 @@ static int log_conflicting_inodes(struct btrfs_trans_handle *trans,
 				  struct btrfs_root *root,
 				  struct btrfs_log_ctx *ctx)
 {
+	const bool orig_log_new_dentries = ctx->log_new_dentries;
 	int ret = 0;
 
 	/*
@@ -6256,7 +6257,11 @@ static int log_conflicting_inodes(struct btrfs_trans_handle *trans,
 			 * dir index key range logged for the directory. So we
 			 * must make sure the deletion is recorded.
 			 */
+			ctx->log_new_dentries = false;
 			ret = btrfs_log_inode(trans, inode, LOG_INODE_ALL, ctx);
+			if (!ret && ctx->log_new_dentries)
+				ret = log_new_dir_dentries(trans, inode, ctx);
+
 			btrfs_add_delayed_iput(inode);
 			if (ret)
 				break;
@@ -6291,6 +6296,7 @@ static int log_conflicting_inodes(struct btrfs_trans_handle *trans,
 			break;
 	}
 
+	ctx->log_new_dentries = orig_log_new_dentries;
 	ctx->logging_conflict_inodes = false;
 	if (ret)
 		free_conflicting_inodes(ctx);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies the file `fs/btrfs/tree-log.c` to fix a bug where new directory entries (dentries) were not being logged when logging the parent directory of a conflicting inode. The key changes occur in the function `log_conflicting_inodes`:

1. **Preserve the original `log_new_dentries` flag**: The function saves the current value of `ctx->log_new_dentries` into a local variable (`orig_log_new_dentries`) before modifying it.

2. **Disable new dentry logging during conflict inode logging**: Before calling `btrfs_log_inode` for the conflicting inode, `ctx->log_new_dentries` is set to `false`. This prevents the logging of new dentries during the initial log of the conflicting inode itself.

3. **Conditionally log new dentries after logging the conflicting inode**: After successfully logging the conflicting inode, if `ctx->log_new_dentries` has been set to `true` (indicating that new dentries were found and need to be logged), the function calls `log_new_dir_dentries` to actually log those new dentries. This ensures that when the parent directory is logged due to a conflicting inode, its new dentries are also recorded.

4. **Restore the original flag**: After processing all conflicting inodes, `ctx->log_new_dentries` is restored to its original value (`orig_log_new_dentries`) so that subsequent operations behave correctly.

The relationship between these modifications is that they ensure a complete and correct log of the parent directory when logging a conflicting inode. Without these changes, the parent directory would be marked as logged but its new dentries would be omitted, leading to data loss after a power failure if the directory was later fsynced without further modifications.
